clue.text: Strip club number

parts.note: a cricket or baseball club is a bat
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A dance act at a seedy strip club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip club' reads as one phrase, but 'Strip' is the definition and 'club number' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A batten is a long thin strip of wood used in building.

clue.text: Poet's written about Flanders, heading off for post at sea

indicators.note: the poet's word is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: a bard is a poet

indicators.note: the name loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: Moll Flanders is Defoe's heroine

explanation.surface: A war poet wrote of Flanders before heading to a naval post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flanders' suggests the battlefields; it is Defoe's Moll, which loses its head to give OLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bollard is a post on a quay or ship for mooring lines.

clue.text: Bulging belly with blocked tubes, it's said

indicators.note: spoken with a blocked nose, the M sounds come out as B

parts.note: a tummy is a belly

explanation.surface: A swollen belly comes with clogged pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: The blocked tubes are nasal passages: with a cold, the word for belly is pronounced with Bs for Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubby means plump, with a round bulging middle.

clue.text: Early Europeans cast runes, when uncertain

indicators.note: uncertain letters are unsettled, so they fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Ancient peoples consulting runes when unsure of the future.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were an ancient people of central Italy before Rome.

clue.text: Uproar as facilities limited by regressive cut

indicators.note: the facilities are hemmed in, bounded on both sides, by the cut
going backwards, so the word for cut is read from its end

parts.note: to reap is to cut a crop
facilities is a euphemism for a toilet, a lav

explanation.surface: A row breaks out because toilets have been restricted by backward-looking cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facilities' sounds like amenities in general; British English uses it coyly for toilets. 'regressive' makes PAER, read backwards, which holds the toilet word.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver means a fuss or commotion, a near synonym of uproar.

clue.text: Byzantine Empire's assumption

indicators.note: byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are tangled up

parts.note: here the apostrophe S supplies a letter, giving the word empires

explanation.surface: The Byzantine Empire's presumption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Byzantine Empire' reads as history; 'Byzantine' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A premise is a proposition assumed as the basis of an argument.

clue.text: Catch girl brooding?

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a brooding bird sits on an egg, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Grab the moody girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brooding' looks like moody; it is a hen sitting, the girl on top of an egg (O).
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso is to catch an animal with a looped rope.

clue.text: Hate-filled violent riot during civil disorder

indicators.note: one piece sits within the time of the other, so inside it
the letters of civil are thrown into confusion
a violent riot has its letters thrown about

explanation.surface: A vicious riot erupting amid civil unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'violent riot' and 'civil disorder' both read as plain news phrases, yet each first word is an anagram signal; 'violent' gives TRIO and the civil letters wrap around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic speech is full of bitter hatred.

clue.text: Rudd's overnight flight?

definitions.meaning: the rudd is a freshwater fish
a night flight that leaves passengers bleary

explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye is both a name for the rudd fish and a nickname for an overnight plane journey.

clue.text: Hairy man's sanctimonious daughter

parts.note: his is the man's possessive
pi is short for pious, meaning sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A man's holier-than-thou daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispid is a botanical term for covered in bristles, that is hairy.

clue.text: Reprobate Wooster briefly in bosom of family

indicators.note: something held in the bosom sits in the middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a line is a family lineage

indicators.note: a thing said briefly is cut short, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Bertie Wooster is P G Wodehouse's comic hero

explanation.surface: Wodehouse's Bertie, a bit of a rogue, being hugged by his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster is the foppish narrator of the Jeeves stories; 'briefly' drops his name's last letter to give BERTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a dissolute person, much the same as a reprobate.

clue.text: Stuffed with chopped dates

indicators.note: chopped up dates are cut into pieces and rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe filled with chopped dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Sated means full up, like someone stuffed after a big meal.

clue.text: Front half of cat only — it has no bottom

indicators.note: the opening five of the ten letters of the cat breed are kept

parts.note: the Abyssinian is a breed of cat

explanation.surface: Only the front part of a cat, so it has no bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is not given as letters: think of the breed ABYSSINIAN and keep its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a chasm thought of as bottomless.

clue.text: It may cause rash woman to pursue tipple

indicators.note: the woman comes after the drink, chasing it

parts.note: 'what's your poison?' asks what you like to drink, so poison is a tipple
Ivy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman chasing a drink may be acting rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like an adjective about the woman; it is a skin rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact with this plant brings the skin out in an itchy rash.

clue.text: Ace place to find fish fingers?

parts.note: the dab is a small flatfish
fingers are found on the hand, the clue's 'place to find' them

explanation.surface: Where would you find a fish's fingers?
explanation.walkthrough: A fish has no hands, which is the joke: the dab's hand is the 'place to find fish fingers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is an expert, someone who is an ace at something.

clue.text: Future wife belatedly beginning crash diet to fit into dress

indicators.note: only the opening letter of belatedly is used
the crashed diet must squeeze inside the dress

parts.note: a robe is a dress

indicators.note: crash is taken as smash up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A future bride belatedly starts a crash diet to fit into her wedding dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash diet' reads as one phrase, but 'crash' is the anagram signal, giving IDET; 'belatedly beginning' just means its first letter, not 'starting late'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman engaged to be married will soon be a wife.

clue.text: He'd bib ale not primarily fit for consumption

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its first, primary, letter

explanation.surface: A drinker in a bib downing ale, with doubts about whether it is drinkable.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letters of He'd, bib and ale leaves ED, IB and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edible can safely be eaten.

clue.text: Around Christmas nurse's chaotic party ends in unseemly behaviour

parts.note: Christmas comes in December, abbreviated Dec, so around then is in Dec
EN is an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: the last letters of chaotic and party are taken

explanation.surface: A nurse's wild Christmas party ends in bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' is not a container; with Christmas it means IN DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecency is improper, offensive conduct.

clue.text: Dutch beauty queen?

definitions.meaning: in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' is a man's wife
... is the title of an American beauty queen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like a nationality before 'beauty queen'; it is the Cockney word for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is informal for a wife, as is Cockney Dutch; split, it gives Miss US, a pageant winner.

clue.text: Beaten, Romney enters Senate

indicators.note: the politician goes inside the abbreviation for Senate

parts.note: Sen is the abbreviation for Senate
Mitt Romney is a US politician

explanation.surface: Defeated in the election, Romney moves to the Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten is the past participle of smite, to strike, so beaten.

clue.text: A bit tight-lipped about being responsible following overdraft

indicators.note: the tight-lipped word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent

indicators.note: the letters for being responsible come after the overdraft

parts.note: OD is the bank abbreviation for overdrawn
IC stands for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone keeping quiet about being to blame for running up an overdraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small amount, just a bit of something.

clue.text: Risk being regularly engulfed by tear gas

indicators.note: the picked letters are swallowed inside the gas

parts.note: Mace is a brand of tear gas spray

indicators.note: every other letter of being is taken

explanation.surface: The danger of being repeatedly overcome by tear gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of being, EN.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat or danger, a risk.

clue.text: Butter in fruit, reportedly

indicators.note: the word for the fruit is spoken, its sound giving the answer

parts.note: the medlar is a small brown fruit

explanation.surface: Butter spread in a fruit dish, as reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts in.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddler interferes in others' affairs, one who butts in.

clue.text: Furious to find rat in fast food

parts.note: hot under the collar means furious
a rat and a dog are both terms for a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Someone livid to discover a rat in their takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a sausage in a bun, sold as fast food.

clue.text: No atropine used during surgery

parts.note: none is nought, the letter O

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in a new order

explanation.surface: An operation carried out without the drug atropine.
explanation.walkthrough: Only O comes from 'No' (nought); with ATROPINE it rearranges to the answer. 'during' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a piece of surgery.

clue.text: Scotsman kicking drug, becoming strict Protestant

indicators.note: kicking a drug habit means giving it up, so the letter goes

parts.note: Hamish is a typical Scottish man's name
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A Scot gives up drugs and joins a strict church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a strict Protestant sect living simply.

clue.text: Prize setter, to many a sex god

parts.note: a cup is a trophy or prize
the setter refers to herself as I
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: A crossword setter winning a prize is a sex god to her fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid is the Roman god of erotic love.

clue.text: Picture books' decorative border

parts.note: pic is short for picture
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A picture book's ornamental edging.
explanation.definitionFit: Picot is a small ornamental loop forming an edging on lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Italian cathedrals arouse odium

indicators.note: to stir up the word odium is to shake its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Italy's churches provoke hatred.
explanation.definitionFit: Duomo is Italian for a cathedral; duomi is its plural.

clue.text: Industrial and kind of foul

definitions.meaning: in basketball a ... foul is given for unsporting conduct

explanation.definitionFit: Technical means relating to applied science and industry, and names a basketball penalty.

clue.text: Dull, hard, faceless men make female grouse

parts.note: grey means dull and dreary
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: without its face, the word men loses its front letter

explanation.surface: Dreary, tough, anonymous men turn into a hen grouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The greyhen is the female of the black grouse.

clue.text: Playboy stereotypically gobbling reputed aphrodisiac

indicators.note: the two words swallow the answer, holding it inside

explanation.surface: The stereotypical playboy wolfs down oysters for their famed effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are said by folklore to stir sexual desire.
